questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What word describes a sudden shaking of the ground caused by moving tectonic plates?
questions.why: An earthquake happens when built-up stress at a plate boundary is suddenly released, shaking the ground.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 72°. What is its alternate angle, in degrees?
questions.why: Alternate angles are equal, so the alternate angle is also 72°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has all sides equal length but no right angles. How many equal sides does it have?
questions.why: This describes a rhombus — all 4 sides are equal, but the angles don't have to be 90°, unlike a square.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A parallelogram has one angle of 70°. What is the size of its opposite angle, in degrees?
questions.why: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are always equal, so the opposite angle is also 70°.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these steps of historical analysis from first to last
questions.why: Historians first gather evidence, then work out causes, then trace consequences, and finally judge what changed or stayed the same over time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is the name for a giant sea wave caused by an underwater earthquake?
questions.why: A tsunami is a series of huge waves triggered when an underwater earthquake displaces a large volume of water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What structural feature helps a building sway safely instead of cracking during an earthquake?
questions.why: Base isolators or dampers let a building flex and absorb shaking, rather than rigidly resisting it and cracking.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A classmate says the Battle of Hastings in 1066 'caused' the entire feudal system, as if nothing before it mattered. Explain why historians would push back on treating one event as the sole cause of such a big, long-term change.
